description:
How does a tiny seed grow into a big plant? Gizmo the robot opens a seed in his lab, watches it wake up under the ground and follows it all the way to a flower. A gentle science lesson for ages 4-8 with questions to answer, things to count and a quiz at the end.
Kids learn the three parts of a seed (a tiny baby plant, its food and the seed coat), that a seed needs water, air and the right warmth to start growing, that the root comes out first and grows down while the shoot grows up, that leaves make the plant's food with sunlight, air and water, that roots take in water, and that flowers help plants make new seeds.

title: How Do Rockets Fly? Science for Kids with Gizmo
description:
How do rockets fly? Find out with Gizmo the robot: a rocket engine turns its fuel into hot gas and pushes it out the back, and the gas pushes the rocket the other way. A rocket carries its own oxygen, so it works in space, and big rockets drop empty stages to get lighter.
A science explainer for kids ages 4-8, with questions to answer, things to copy, quick checks and a quiz at the end.

title: Where Does Rain Come From? Science for Kids with Gizmo
description:
Where does rain come from? Find out with Gizmo the robot: the sun warms water and turns some of it into invisible water vapor, cold air high up turns the vapor back into tiny drops that gather on specks of dust and make clouds, and drops that grow too heavy fall as rain. Small raindrops are round and bigger ones are shaped like a hamburger bun.
A science explainer for kids ages 4-8, with questions to answer, things to copy, quick checks and a quiz at the end.

Where the facts come from (read Nov 19, 2026): USGS Water Science School, The Water Cycle for Kids and Are Raindrops Shaped Like Teardrops?; NOAA SciJinks, What Causes Rain?
